scenes.tts: Every cell with a nucleus, from yeast to you, runs its cycle on one engine. The engine is a kinase called a C D K, a cyclin-dependent kinase. Alone, it does nothing. It switches on only when a partner protein, a cyclin, is bound. The cell builds cyclin up, the kinase switches on, and the next step begins. Then the cell destroys the cyclin, the kinase switches off, and the cycle resets.
scenes.visual: A yeast cell and a human cell side by side share one engine icon. A CDK blob with a closed site docks a cyclin and lights up; the cyclin is then chopped and the CDK goes dark. Two traces below: flat CDK, sawtooth cyclin.
scenes.narration: Every cell with a nucleus, from yeast to you, runs its cycle on one engine. The engine is a kinase called a CDK, a cyclin-dependent kinase. Alone, it does nothing. It switches on only when a partner protein, a cyclin, is bound. The cell builds cyclin up, the kinase switches on, and the next step begins. Then the cell destroys the cyclin, the kinase switches off, and the cycle resets.

scenes.tts: Different cyclins rise at different times. Cyclin D works in G one, cyclin E drives the move from G one into S, and cyclin B with C D K one drives mitosis. That is the usual pattern, not a strict rule.
scenes.visual: A ring of G1, S, G2 and M with cyclin D, cyclin E and cyclin B peaks rising in turn at their phases; a small tag reads 'usual pattern'.
scenes.narration: Different cyclins rise at different times. Cyclin D works in G1, cyclin E drives the move from G1 into S, and cyclin B with CDK1 drives mitosis. That is the usual pattern, not a strict rule.

scenes.tts: The engine has brakes. Wee one puts an inhibitory phosphate on C D K one, and C D C twenty-five takes it off. Inhibitor proteins can also bind and block. Active C D K one switches on its activator and switches off its brake, so once mitosis starts, it goes all the way.
scenes.visual: Wee1 clips a phosphate onto CDK1, Cdc25 removes it; an inhibitor wraps the kinase; then arrows from active CDK1 back to Cdc25 (on) and Wee1 (off), and a step-shaped switch flips to 'mitosis'.
scenes.narration: The engine has brakes. Wee1 puts an inhibitory phosphate on CDK1, and Cdc25 takes it off. Inhibitor proteins can also bind and block. Active CDK1 switches on its activator and switches off its brake, so once mitosis starts, it goes all the way.

scenes.tts: Checkpoints decide when the brakes stay on. In G one, a cell commits only if it has enough nutrients and growth factors. If DNA is damaged or not fully copied, checkpoint signals act on Wee one and C D C twenty-five, and the cell waits in G two. In mitosis, a checkpoint holds back destruction until every chromosome is attached.
scenes.visual: Three gates on the cycle ring: G1 gate with nutrient and growth-factor icons; G2 gate where a broken DNA strand holds the Wee1 brake on; M gate where one unattached chromosome holds back the APC/C.
scenes.narration: Checkpoints decide when the brakes stay on. In G1, a cell commits only if it has enough nutrients and growth factors. If DNA is damaged or not fully copied, checkpoint signals act on Wee1 and Cdc25, and the cell waits in G2. In mitosis, a checkpoint holds back destruction until every chromosome is attached.

scenes.tts: Destruction makes the cycle run one way. A ubiquitin ligase, the A P C slash C, tags securin, so sister chromatids can separate, and then cyclin B, which ends mitosis. A cyclin that cannot be destroyed holds a frog egg extract in mitosis. Making cyclin drives entry. Destroying it permits exit.
scenes.visual: APC/C tags securin, sisters separate, then tags cyclin B and the CDK goes dark. Inset tube: a cyclin with a lock symbol stays high and the extract stays in mitosis.

scenes.tts: The engine explains an old puzzle. Fuse a cell that is copying its DNA with one that has not started, and the second nucleus starts early. Fuse it with one that has finished, and that nucleus refuses. A genome is copied once per cycle.
scenes.visual: Two cells fuse; the unstarted nucleus starts copying, the finished one stays dark with a 'copied' stamp until a mitosis icon passes and clears it.
scenes.narration: The engine explains an old puzzle. Fuse a cell that is copying its DNA with one that has not started, and the second nucleus starts early. Fuse it with one that has finished, and that nucleus refuses. A genome is copied once per cycle.

scenes.tts: Three lines of work found the engine. Frog oocytes gave an activity, M P F. Yeast mutants gave the gene C D C two. Sea urchins gave cyclin. Then the lines met: M P F is C D C two, now called C D K one, bound to cyclin B.
scenes.visual: Three threads labelled frog oocyte (MPF), yeast (cdc2) and sea urchin (cyclin) converge into one CDK1-cyclin B complex.
scenes.narration: Three lines of work found the engine. Frog oocytes gave an activity, MPF. Yeast mutants gave the gene Cdc2. Sea urchins gave cyclin. Then the lines met: MPF is Cdc2, now called CDK1, bound to cyclin B.
